questions.question:

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. At this speed the rocket soon attained the height of 190 miles above the earth.

B. At 9 am the great rocket lifted in the air with a mighty roar.

C. It rose smoothly at first, then quickened to a speed of 17,5 00 miles an hour.

D. Gagarin now pulled himself towards the window to look down.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 3.**
 
• The given jumbled sentences are talking about the launch of a rocket. So the answer begins with sentence B as it is talking about the beginning of the rocket launch. Sentences C & A make paired sentences, as C is talking about the speed & is continued by sentence A. 
 
• This sequence is correctly followed by option 3 'BCAD'.

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

Mrs. Sangeeta Malik is one of the favourite teacher of most children in our school.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. one of the favourite teacher.**

 
• A **plural** noun is used after** 'one of the'.**
 
• Hence, **'teachers'** will be used in the given sentence.

So, the correct sentence will be:** Mrs. Sangeeta Malik is one of the favourite teachers of most children in our school.**

**Note: Most** can be used as a** determiner, **in general**,** to refer to **a quantity of an unspecific group of people or things.**

**E.g. Most** students ask questions.

There is no need for placing article '**the'** in this situation. So there is no error in the last part of the sentence.

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

Father said to me, "Are you going to keep me waiting all night?'

options.text: Father told me that you are going to keep him waiting all night.
Father asked me if I was going to keep him waiting all night.
Father asked me if you were going to keep him waiting all night.
Father asked me are you going to keep me waiting all night.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e. Father asked me if I was going keep him waiting all night.**

 
• If the **direct** speech is in the** interrogative** form, **'said to'** is changed into **'asked'.**
 
• The subject in the reported speech i.e.** **'you' is changed according to the object i.e. me of the reporting speech.
 
• Hence,** 'you'** will be changed into **'I'**.
 
• And the auxiliary verb in indirect speech will be used according to 'I' i.e.** was.**
 
• All these rules are followed in option 2), hence, it will be the correct answer.

The correct answer is **option 4) i.e. found violating the law.**

• 'find' is always followed by** 'V4'.** 
 
• Hence, in the given sentence** 'violating'** will be used in place of **'violated'.**
 
• So, the sentence after improvement will be: **The civic bodies in the capital have formed teams to crack down on coaching centres found violating the law.**

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. The subjects taught in the Gurukul varied from Sanskrit to Mathematics.

B. Indian education has its roots in the ancient ages.

C. However this system changed when the British ca me to India.

D. In those days the Gurukul system was followed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. BDCA.

A can not be the first sentence because this follows part D.

C starts with contradictory conjunction so, this will not be the first sentence.

D follows Part B.

So, the first sentence will be part B. As B is followed by D so BD will be a combination and this is in the option A so this will be our correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 1.**
 
• The correct pronoun to be used in the given blank is 'they' as we are talking about two persons in the passage. The pronoun 'they' is used when referring to more than one person.
 
• Option 2 is wrong because the pronoun 'we' is used to refer to different groups of people, but always including the speaker.
 
• Option 3 'them' is wrong because it is the accusative form of 'they', which is used to show the direct object of a verb. 
 
• Option 4 'she' is wrong as it is a singular pronoun whereas we require plural pronoun to fit in the blank.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
